newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union boss calls for limits on foreigners.
newsitem.headline: German union boss calls for limits on foreigners.

text.p: Klaus Zwickel, the chairman of Germany's largest union IG Metall, has added his voice to calls by conservative politicians for stricter limits on foreign workers, a German magazine reported on Sunday.

"I really think we must come to agreed quotas (on foreign workers) within an immigration law to relieve the German labour market and to diffuse social tension," Zwickel said in an interview with Focus weekly magazine, according to an advance releaseD ahead of publication on Monday.
Earlier this month the conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) called for stricter limits on foreign workers as part of a new strategy to cut unemployment.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, chairman of the Bavarian sister party to Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), said it was "grotesque" that millions of Germans were unemployed while so many foreigners were working here.

Major parties and unions had long refrained from directly linking the over 10 percent record unemployment level to the country's eight million foreign residents, in part because they want to avoid being accused of stirring up racial unrest.
